## Investigation and hypothesis

I read both complete original history rows and JSON, the first-tier actual
short split source/replay/results, full current target diff and explain,
whole-group report, actual Cord_Get_Small source and retail listing, both
helpers' actual caller results, current callers' inline source, exact
Key_Exchange, ACK1 conversion splits, ACK2 and PumpConnections lifetime forms.
Retail direct caller search finds zero calls to either out-of-line Get helper;
the C++ callers inline the helpers into packet parsing. This does not license
changing parsing semantics or rebuilding their unmatched callers separately.

The first-tier input split only the short-path input read/ntohs. The long path
still had an actual `ntohl(*value)` argument read after its required raw store.
ACK1's successful all-five-splits combination supplied a demonstrated new
function-wide conversion lever: independently ineffective local splits can
interact. Root approved testing that precise remaining long conversion and
its combination with the already tested short split. This was a source-level
allocation hypothesis, not evidence that ACK1 guarantees the same outcome.

Both candidates keep `*value = *(unsigned int *)in` in its original place.
They then read that actual *value into an unsigned int, convert the local with
the existing ntohl call, mask and perform the existing final output store.
The combined candidate also splits the short input load/ntohs. Each operation
occurs once and both real long-path stores remain; potential input/output
aliasing therefore sees the same order. No fake objects, padding, volatile,
extra output stores, clock changes or dead reads were introduced. Physical
line counts and the runner's assertion/log guard pass.

## Limits, rejected directions and reopening

Original history has 12 compiled forms but no stash or exact input patches.
It covers direct stores, unsigned-short locals, output pointer/reference types,
casts/masks, result locals, branch forms, pointer copies and store-then-ntohs.
Whether an unavailable old source also included this exact long split remains
unknown. The later zero-form behavior review is not a compiler attempt. The
Terra short-only input and these two Sol inputs are available exact sources;
all three newly documented inputs produce the same target body.

Cord_Get_Small is an exact neighboring helper, but it returns a one-byte value
on the branch where Get_Seq needs two, and masks its other path to 15 bits.
Substituting it would change sequence decoding. Its output width and required
pre-call store also make it a poor claim of an equivalent short-path schedule.
ACK2's real object lifetime and PumpConnections' helper construction fix stack
allocation for new/add/delete sequences; this scalar helper contains no such
object or sequence. Introducing a wrapper, scalar-copy memcpy or invented
temporary solely to disturb scheduling has no additional client-supported
helper evidence here. Extra raw short-path output stores would contradict the
retail operation sequence. Further pointer/local/cast permutations overlap the
documented old search and have no new demonstrated mechanism after duplicates.

I identified no distinct supported followup after inspecting these actual
outputs. This is bounded exhaustion after the one useful batch, not a claim
that every equivalent C++ program was searched or an arbitrary input quota.
Reopen on recovered original-source structure, a demonstrated existing scalar
helper/interface that preserves the exact reads/stores and shifts output
pointer loading relative to zero-extension, or another independently proven
function-wide mechanism applicable to this helper. A new model alone is not
that evidence. Root may route the actual records to authorized Astra review.
